channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Samaje Perine rushed six times for 14 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 10 win over the Steelers, adding 25 yards on four receptions.
item.description: Perine’s 10 touches dwarfed in comparison to the 18 of lead back Chase Brown, the latter of whom found the end zone twice for his second and third scores of the season. Low weekly volume in the pass-first Cincinnati offense leaves Perine nothing more than a desperation Flex without an injury ahead of him on the depth chart.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Mike Gesicki caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Bengals’ Week 10 win over the Steelers.
item.description: Gesicki caught the first pass from scrimmage for nine yards before completely disappearing the rest of the game, which was easy to do considering Ja’Marr Chase erupted for the third highest receiving total in a game in his career with 231 yards. The Steelers just had no answer for the elite alpha receiver, leaving little scraps leftover for the rest of the Cincinnati offense. The only thing Chase didn’t do was find the end zone, with the touchdowns accounted for by Chase Brown (two), Samaje Perine, Dohnte Meyers, and Drew Sample. Gesicki remains a touchdown-dependent TE2 ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Commanders on Monday Night Football.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Dohnte Meyers caught both targets for 20 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 10 win over the Steelers.
item.description: Meyers capped off the second quarter with a touchdown reception from 15 yards out and only nine seconds remaining before the half. He would not be targeted again as the Bengals leaned heavily on Ja’Marr Chase on their way to a blowout win, with their defense holding the Steelers to 23 yards of total offense through the first three quarters of play. Meyers remains a desperation Flex ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Commanders on Monday Night Football.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Tee Higgins caught 5-of-6 targets for 66 yards in the Bengals’ Week 10 win over the Steelers.
item.description: Higgins’ six targets finished third on the team behind Ja’Marr Chase (14) and Chase Brown (nine) while his receiving output was dwarfed by the 231 yards of Chase. The matchup against the zone-heavy Steelers likely played a significant role in the target breakout, with Higgins much more dangerous against man coverage this season. Higgins remains an elite WR2 ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Commanders on Monday Night Football.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Chase Brown rushed 10 times for 44 yards in the Bengals’ Week 10 win over the Steelers, adding 39 yards and two touchdowns on eight receptions.
item.description: Brown continues to see a modest workload on the ground playing in the offense leading the league in pass rate over expectation while averaging almost 38 pass attempts per game. The pass game usage isn’t reliable on a weekly basis despite the veteran back seeing nine or more targets on three separate occasions this season. This was also his first game with a trip to the end zone since Week 1 despite working as a borderline workhorse this season, leaving Brown as an upside RB2 ahead of a Week 11 matchup against the pass-funnel Commanders, where he’ll likely require elite pass game utilization to return a usable score on that valuation.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Ja’Marr Chase caught 11-of-14 targets for 231 yards in the Bengals’ Week 10 win over the Steelers.
item.description: It was the second consecutive game in which Chase went over 140 yards in the first half alone, eventually notching the third most receiving yards in a game in his illustrious career with 231 while blowing by the century mark for the third consecutive contest. Chase was the primary point of emphasis from the first kick against the Steelers, working mostly the short-to-intermediate areas of the field before bomb on a sluggo route in the second quarter. He worked behind primary coverage on three separate instances but was ushered out of bounds on all three occasions, any of which would have further inflated his counting stats had they turned into touchdowns. Chase and the Bengals now get a long week of preparation for the pass-funnel Commanders on Monday Night Football in Week 11, where he will remain an elite WR1.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Joe Burrow completed 35-of-44 passes for 409 yards and four touchdowns in the Bengals’ 38-18, Week 10 win over the Steelers, adding eight yards on one carry.
item.description: Burrow cruised to his fifth consecutive game of four total touchdowns or more, passing for 302 yards and three scores in the first half alone. The Steelers were completely unable to move the ball consistently while managing only 23 yards of total offense through the first three quarters, allowing Burrow and the Bengals to build an insurmountable lead through the first 45 minutes of play. The win sends Cincinnati to the top of the AFC North with a 7-2 record after splitting the season series with the Steelers, now in the driver’s seat for the division title with two months remaining in the regular season. Burrow will look to keep the elite play going in a Week 11 meeting with the pass-funnel Commanders on Monday Night Football, where he remains a top tier QB1 in fantasy circles.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Germie Bernard did not catch any of his three targets in the Steelers’ Week 10 loss to the Bengals, gaining 10 yards on one carry.
item.description: Bernard has now had three modest fantasy showings after his breakout game against the Buccaneers, failing to eclipse 30 yards in all three outings since Week 6. His output against the Bengals is more a microcosm of the performance from the entire Pittsburgh offense, a unit that gained only 23 yards of total offense through the first 45 minutes of play while losing 17 yards on two third quarter possessions. Fantasy managers that thought they found a hidden gem on the waiver wire a month ago have little to show for it and must question whether to start the rookie receiver in a middling matchup against the reeling Eagles in Week 11.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Pat Freiermuth caught 2-of-3 targets for 35 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 10 loss to the Bengals.
item.description: This was one to forget for the entire Pittsburgh offense, who managed to gain just 23 yards of total offense through the first three quarters of play, limiting the fantasy production of all parties involved. Freiermuth was one of two fortunate ones to salvage his fantasy day with a fourth quarter touchdown when the game was already well out of reach, although the modest reception and yardage totals were far too familiar for Freiermuth’s fantasy managers. He’ll remain a touchdown-or-bust TE2 ahead of a Week 11 matchup with the Eagles.-Mark Garcia

item.title: DK Metcalf caught 2-of-6 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 10 loss to the Bengals.
item.description: Metcalf was blanked through three quarters as the offense was held to a paltry 23 yards of total offense in the first 45 minutes of play. He salvaged his fantasy day with two receptions for 54 yards and a touchdown on the team’s first possession of the final frame, tacking on a two-point conversion for good measure. Even so, Metcalf has been one of fantasy’s bigger disappointments this season, with just 432 yards and two touchdowns through nine games played, while also catching under 50 percent of his targets. Even worse is the fact that he has only three receptions of 20 yards or more this season. Metcalf will remain a shaky FLEX ahead of a Week 11 meeting with the Eagles.-Mark Garcia
